title: cornus kousa subsp. chinensis
intro: Cornus kousa subsp. chinensis, commonly known as Chinese dogwood, is a deciduous shrub or small tree native to East Asia, characterized by its showy white or pink flowers and red berries. The plant has been traditionally used in Chinese medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues, due to its numerous health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Chinese dogwood include analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic effects, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids. The plant's bioactive constituents also include coumarins, which have been shown to exhibit antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.
